explanation: Only the number of long planks affects the total; the ordering of those planks does not. For k long planks, total length is planks*shorter+k*(longer-shorter). Enumerating k from zero through planks covers all choices without exploring 2^planks arrangements. Equal plank lengths collapse all counts to one answer.
correctness: Every board uses a unique count k of long planks between zero and planks, so its total has the stated formula. Conversely every such k is feasible by choosing k long planks and the rest short. When longer>shorter, increasing k strictly increases the total, proving the generated list is sorted and contains no duplicates. When lengths agree, all choices yield the single emitted total. The k=0 empty-board case yields zero.
walkthrough: For 3 planks of lengths 2 and 5, choose 0,1,2,3 long planks to get 6,9,12,15. Short-long-short and long-short-short both have length 9 and appear once. With equal lengths 2 and 2, only 6 is returned.
timeComplexity: O(planks+1) time when lengths differ, matching output size; O(1) when equal.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space excluding the returned O(planks+1) integer values, or one value for equal lengths.
edgeCases: Zero planks, equal lengths, one plank.
Maximum count and lengths, without integer overflow or duplicate totals.
